Which of the following correctly lists all eight compass points in clockwise order starting from North?  
A) N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW  
B) N, NW, W, SW, S, SE, E, NE  
C) N, E, S, W, NE, SE, SW, NW  
D) N, NE, NW, E, W, SE, SW, S
a

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

A bearing is always measured clockwise from which direction?
A) East
B) South
C) North
D) West
c

Correct — nice work. Try this one:

What is the bearing equivalent of the compass point Southwest (SW)?
A) 135°
B) 225°
C) 315°
D) 45°
b

Yes, exactly right. Next up:

A marine navigation challenge gives you three compass points: East-Southeast (ESE), South-Southwest (SSW), and West-Northwest (WNW). Which list best represents their approximate bearings in ascending order?
A) 112.5°, 202.5°, 292.5°
B) 67.5°, 157.5°, 247.5°
C) 157.5°, 247.5°, 337.5°
D) 22.5°, 112.5°, 202.5°
a

That's it — well done. Here's another:

A bearing of 315° corresponds to which compass point?
A) Northeast (NE)
B) Northwest (NW)
C) Southeast (SE)
D) Southwest (SW)
b

Good morning! Today you'll learn why angles on a straight line always add up to 180° and how to use this to find missing angles.

Imagine standing on Mahé's eastern shore watching the sun rise and set along the horizon. Two angles on a straight line are 80° and 100°. What is their sum?
morning! ok so 80 plus 100... that's 180. yeah they add up to 180.

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

One angle on a straight line is 60°. Find the other angle.
ok so if one is 60 and they add up to 180, then the other one is 180 minus 60... that's 120.

Correct — nice work. Try this one:

Two angles on a straight line are 80° and 100°. What is their sum?
80 plus 100 is 180.

Yes, exactly right. Next up:

One angle on a straight line is 110°. What is the other angle?
180 minus 110 is 70.

That's it — well done. Here's another:

Two straight lines intersect. One angle formed is 90°. What is the vertically opposite angle?
wait, vertically opposite? um... i think that's the one across from it yeah? so it's also 90.

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

Two straight lines intersect, forming four angles. One angle is 120°. What is the angle adjacent to it on the straight line?
ok so if one angle is 120 and they're on a straight line, then 180 minus 120 is 60.

Correct — nice work. Try this one:

Three angles on a straight line measure 45°, 70°, and x°. What is x?

hmm wait, three angles on a straight line? so they all add up to 180 right?

45 plus 70 is 115, then 180 minus 115 is 65. so x is 65.

Yes, exactly right. Next up:

At a market stall in Victoria, a shop owner positions a shade cloth on a straight line frame. The frame is divided by support poles into angles of 28°, 95°, and y. Find y.
ok so all three angles add up to 180 on the straight line. 28 plus 95 is 123, then 180 minus 123 is 57. so y is 57.

That's it — well done. Here's another:

Two intersecting lines form four angles. One angle is 120°. What is the angle adjacent to it on the straight line?
180 minus 120 is 60.

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

Three angles around a point are 100°, 120°, and x°. Find x.
wait, around a point? is that different from on a straight line?

Not quite — let's walk through it together. Angles on a straight line always add up to exactly 180° (they form a half-turn).  
Angles around a single point always add up to exactly 360° (they form a full turn).

The question you are answering now is about angles **around a point**, so the three given angles plus x must total 360°.

Add the two known angles (100° + 120°), then tell me what you subtract from 360° to find x.
oh right, around a point is 360. so 100 plus 120 is 220, then 360 minus 220 is 140. so x is 140.

In Seychelles, our granite islands are constantly shaped by the ocean, sun, and rain. Welcome! Today you'll learn how to read and write grid references so you can navigate maps like a true Seychellois explorer.

On a standard map grid, which of the following correctly describes the order in which you read a four-figure grid reference?  
A) Northing first (vertical), then easting second (horizontal)  
B) Easting first (horizontal), then northing second (vertical)  
C) Easting and northing simultaneously from the center of the square  
D) Northing first, then easting, then a compass direction

**Answer with the letter (A, B, C or D).**
b

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

What does a grid reference of 5678 tell you about a location on a map?
A) The exact building within a grid square
B) The entire grid square where the location is found
C) The distance in kilometres from a reference point
D) The direction of travel to reach that location
b

Correct — nice work. Try this one:

A student reads a four-figure grid reference by writing down the northing value before the easting value. For example, they write "3456" instead of "5634". How would this error affect the location identified on the map?
A) The location would be rotated 90 degrees clockwise from the correct position
B) The location would be completely off the map in all cases
C) The location would be in the correct grid square but with rows and columns reversed
D) The location would be reflected across the diagonal axis of the grid
hmm im not sure. is it c?

Yes, exactly right. Next up:

If a four-figure grid reference is 3245, what are the easting and northing values?
A) Easting: 32, Northing: 45
B) Easting: 34, Northing: 25
C) Easting: 3245, Northing: 0000
D) Easting: 45, Northing: 32
a

A) To match the metric system used on all maps
B) To create a decimal system that allows easy estimation of position within the square
C) To represent the scale of the map in kilometres

Imagine sailing from Mahé to an outer island or following a treasure map — today you'll learn to describe directions using both compass points and bearings measured in degrees from North.

Which of the following correctly lists all eight compass points in clockwise order starting from North?  
A) N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW  
B) N, NW, W, SW, S, SE, E, NE  
C) N, E, S, W, NE, SE, SW, NW  
D) N, NE, NW, E, W, SE, SW, S
A

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

A bearing is always measured clockwise from which direction?
A) East
B) South
C) North
D) West
C

Correct — nice work. Try this one:

What is the bearing equivalent of the compass point Southwest (SW)?
A) 135°
B) 225°
C) 315°
D) 45°
B

Yes, exactly right. Next up:

A marine navigation challenge gives you three compass points: East-Southeast (ESE), South-Southwest (SSW), and West-Northwest (WNW). Which list best represents their approximate bearings in ascending order?
A) 112.5°, 202.5°, 292.5°
B) 67.5°, 157.5°, 247.5°
C) 157.5°, 247.5°, 337.5°
D) 22.5°, 112.5°, 202.5°
A

That's it — well done. Here's another:

A bearing of 315° corresponds to which compass point?
A) Northeast (NE)
B) Northwest (NW)
C) Southeast (SE)
D) Southwest (SW)
B

Good morning! Today we'll explore how river channels in Seychelles form different cross-sectional shapes depending on their location and erosion processes.

What do you notice about the differences in how deep and wide each of the three river cross-section profiles is?  
A) They are all identical in depth and width  
B) The upper one is narrow and deep, the middle one is wider and shallower, the lower one is very wide and flat  
C) All three are wide with gentle slopes  
D) They only differ in colour, not shape  

**Answer by typing the letter (A, B, C, or D).**
B

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

Which of the following best describes a V-shaped river channel?
A) Wide and shallow with gentle sloping banks
B) Narrow and deep with steep vertical sides
C) Rectangular in cross-section with uniform depth
D) Broad and flat with extensive floodplain areas
B

Correct — nice work. Try this one:

In the Seychelles context, a small river draining from the higher central peaks typically shows which characteristics?
A) Wide floodplain, U-shaped channel, slow-moving water
B) Steep gradient, V-shaped channel, rapid water flow with vertical erosion
C) Box-shaped channel, moderate gradient, mixed erosion
D) Shallow braided channels with extensive deposition
B

Yes, exactly right. Next up:

Where on a river channel cross-section diagram would you measure the width of the river?
A) From the riverbed to the water surface
B) From one bank to the other bank at the water surface level
C) From the floodplain edge to the opposite floodplain edge
D) Along the longest part of the riverbed
B

That's it — well done. Here's another:

In a river's middle course, which erosion process predominantly shapes the channel into a U-shaped profile?
A) Lateral erosion of the riverbanks by water flowing across the channel
B) Vertical erosion deepening the riverbed through downward cutting
C) Headward erosion extending the river valley upstream
D) Abrasion from sediment particles grinding against bedrock
A

In Seychelles, our granite islands are constantly shaped by the ocean, sun, and rain. Today we'll explore the three main types of weathering: physical, chemical, and biological.

Look at the rocks along Anse Royale beach — some have smooth, rounded surfaces while others show deep cracks and peeling layers. What process is breaking these rocks apart over time?

Which of the following best describes weathering?  
A) The movement of rock particles by wind, water, or ice  
B) The breaking down or disintegration of rocks at or near the Earth's surface  
C) The compaction of sediments into solid rock layers  
D) The melting of rocks deep underground due to high temperatures
B

Got it — that's right. Here's the next one:

Which of the following is the best definition of physical weathering?
A) The breakdown of rock by chemical reactions that change its mineral composition
B) The mechanical breakdown of rock into smaller pieces without changing its chemical composition
C) The weathering of rock caused exclusively by living organisms such as plants and lichens
D) The slow erosion of rock by water movement over thousands of years
B

Correct — nice work. Try this one:

Which of the following is a characteristic that distinguishes chemical weathering from physical weathering?
A) Chemical weathering produces sand and gravel fragments of the original rock
B) Chemical weathering alters the chemical composition and mineral structure of the rock
C) Chemical weathering only occurs in tropical climates with high rainfall
D) Chemical weathering is faster than physical weathering in all environments
B

Yes, exactly right. Next up:

In Seychelles, freeze-thaw weathering is rare because the islands have a tropical climate with consistently warm temperatures. Which of the following best explains why freeze-thaw weathering is more common in mountain regions and high latitudes?
A) Mountains and high latitudes receive less rainfall than tropical islands
B) Temperatures regularly drop below freezing, allowing water in rock cracks to freeze and expand repeatedly
C) The rocks in mountains are softer and more easily broken by ice
D) Chemical weathering does not occur in cold climates, so physical weathering must occur instead
B

That's it — well done. Here's another:

Which of the following is an example of biological weathering?
A) A granite boulder split by a freeze-thaw cycle in a mountain pass
B) A limestone cavern enlarged by carbonic acid in rainwater
C) A concrete pathway broken apart by growing tree roots and colonizing lichens
D) A pebble rounded by repeated tumbling in a river
C
